kind: One run at full size and full length, one seed: the looped stack, trained and scored as the stack arm of full_size_best_rate_pair, beside that pair.
why: full_size_loop_pilot passed. After 24,000 updates on windows of 512 bytes the looped stack (levels 2 to 8 run twice with tied synapses, the pulse budget scaled with the passes) scored 1.31024 on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes: 0.0189 ahead of the plain stack given the same pulses and 0.0096 ahead of the plain stack at the old budget, with gains as large or larger on new contexts. Its record says what that earns: a run of 90,000 updates beside the pair. This is that run. It asks whether the gain holds at full length, on long streams, with knowledge cells and fast output synapses. Every part that helped the stack's knowledge so far helped early and faded with data, and the pilot had a quarter of the updates, on short windows. The gap the loop would have to close is v18's: the best stack is 0.0095 behind the frozen Transformer on test and 0.0188 on validation, 0.0129 and 0.0201 behind the Transformer with fast output synapses.

arms.fsp-loop: the stack arm of full_size_best_rate_pair (fsp-st: v17's recipe l2048-know-st at peak rate 6e-4, 24,000 updates on windows of 512 bytes, then unbroken streams of windows of 2,048 bytes with 128 knowledge cells a head and a reach of 2,048 to update 90,000, one cosine over the run, seed 20001) with --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 in both stages: 18 level passes on the synapses of 11, the budget of 310,000 scaled by 18/11. The loop adds no parameters: 34,810,900 in the first stage and 36,263,956 in the long one, as fsp-st.

base: fsp-st (the plain stack at 6e-4, 310,000 pulses a byte) and fsp-tf (the Transformer at 1.2e-3, 34,752,000 parameters) of full_size_best_rate_pair: the same seed, data, schedule and scoring
training: sched/bin/full-pair3.sh stack fsp-loop 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000: full-pair.sh with trainer flags that join both stages, and with the fast output synapses of the scoring on every pass. Code: the copy of 97a2772, which trained the pilot's fs-loop6; fsp-st trains with the copy of 072eb90, and the three commits between them add noisy thresholds and the lifting pool for them and for gated cells, behind flags that neither run uses. Server GPU 1, from the night of 2026-11-23 after fsp-tf has been scored; about 19 GPU hours, so the run spans two windows by pause and resume.
measure: As full_size_best_rate_pair. The stack is read as a stream over the full enwik8 test and validation splits, at the reach chosen on the first 1,000,000 validation bytes (its trained 2,048 or 8,192), with fast output synapses at 2^24 on the cells of all 18 level passes (taught; fsp-st has 11 levels to hear) and without. It is paired with fsp-st and with fsp-tf piece by piece (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py). Beside the scores: the pulses a byte, the training time, and the share of membrane entries at their bound (experiments/membrane_saturation.py).
reading: (1) The looped stack beats the Transformer at full size if its taught test score is below fsp-tf's frozen score with the paired 95% interval of the gap below zero, and the same holds on validation: the pair's own reading. The gap to fsp-tf with fast output synapses at 0.07 is recorded beside it, and the claim is made without reservation only if it holds against that too. (2) The loop's gain holds at full length if fsp-loop is at least 0.005 better than fsp-st on taught test and on taught validation, each with the paired interval clear of zero; it has faded if it is below 0.003 on either split. The pilot's gain was 0.0096. (3) If the gain holds, the loop is the stack's depth from here on, and the next full-length run goes to the loop variant that a full-size pilot picks (the old budget, the lifting pool, skip fibres if their screen passes). If it has faded, the loop is reported with its curve against the pilot's, and the next full-length run goes to another bet. Recorded either way: every score with and without fast synapses, the gaps to fsp-st and to fsp-tf on both splits with their intervals and their split by context, the pulses a byte (the loop is given 1.63 times the plain stack's, which every claim states), the training time against fsp-st's, and the saturation of the reads, the cells and the other populations.
seen_before_recording: The pilot's scores (full_size_loop_pilot.json). Both arms of the pair are still training and neither is scored: fsp-st was last seen at update 67,500 of 90,000 (1.1433 on the trainer's streams with averaged weights), fsp-tf at 82,500 (1.1298 on its own windows). On the test bed, loop_with_data has its runs of 6,000 updates (loop 1.60491, energy control 1.63019, base 1.62828) and the energy control at 24,000 (1.48591 against the base's 1.48247); the looped bed at 24,000 updates has not trained. No looped stack has trained past 24,000 updates at full size. A launch check of the script's steps ran on the server's CPU at a width of 64 with the loop: 30 updates of the first stage, the fork, 60 updates on streams with knowledge cells, and the scores at the trained reach, at 8,192, and with fast synapses on all 18 passes.
